requirements.title: Defined input/output can override default derived-type data transfer handling
requirements.definition: Defined input/output allows a program to override the default handling of derived-type objects and values in data transfer statements described in 12.6.3.

pending.defined-io-overrides-default-derived-typ: Use a future derived type with a WRITE(FORMATTED) or READ(FORMATTED) defined I/O binding whose child transfer emits or consumes a distinctive nonblank sentinel field; compare with a control that has no defined I/O only after default derived-type handling is registered, and assert the custom transfer effect rather than processor formatting.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or using a compile-only conforming control) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT or named status values where the standard names them, required dummy characteristics through a conforming interface, or required diagnosis of a numbered syntax rule or constraint. Negative plans change one source property from a conforming control and do not require a particular diagnostic message, severity, exit status, printed rule number, IOMSG wording, or processor-dependent numeric status value.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. IOMSG wording and processor-dependent numeric status values are never an oracle. A diagnostic facet is only a future source-control plan when the cited numbered rule alone is violated and the invalid program reaches that rule; unnumbered program restrictions are not assumed to be diagnosed.
requirements.dependencies: Registered dependencies: clauses 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, and existing clause 12/13 catalogues for source form, derived types, generic bindings, expressions, variables, execution constructs, data-transfer statement forms, control information, file positioning, and edit descriptors. Unregistered dependencies explicitly retained: later 12.6 effective-item and data-transfer termination rules; 12.7-12.11 connection, transfer, status, and error semantics; clause 15 interface, generic, type-bound, and argument association rules; clause 16 ISO_FORTRAN_ENV named constants; clause 19 scope and lifetime controls where active parent data transfer statements are reached.

requirements.title: Defined input/output procedures are accessible by a defined-io generic spec and selected by resolution rules
requirements.definition: A defined input/output procedure is a procedure accessible by a defined-io-generic-spec, and a particular defined input/output procedure is selected as described in 12.6.4.8.4.

pending.defined-io-procedure-accessible-by-gener: Compile a conforming module that makes a specific procedure accessible through a READ(FORMATTED) or WRITE(FORMATTED) generic binding or interface, then use a transfer of a nondefault derived-type value to reach that procedure.
pending.defined-io-procedure-selection-by-resolu: Use two conforming specific procedures distinguished by direction/form or dynamic type and record a distinctive child-transfer sentinel from the selected one; assert only the selection rule registered in 12.6.4.8.4.

accounting.rationale: Defines the purpose of defined input/output for derived-type data transfer.
Defines accessibility through a defined-io generic spec and points to the selection rule.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.4.8, defined input/output (batch163). Every unit hash-verified by independent reviewers across two rounds. Round 1 found obligations filed as definitions - the 12.6.4.8.4 resolution rules, and the 12.6.4.8.3 effects that a child data transfer inherits the parent's connection modes, does not position the file, ignores ADVANCE=, associates dtv with the effective item and starts where the file was positioned; all are now requirements with plans in which a DTIO procedure records its observations in module variables with distinguished values. R1221, C1236 and C1237 were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
